texts.name: Subtitle 12
texts.text: Why web-threat detection needs more than one model

texts.name: Point 14
texts.text:
THE BROWSER IS THE ATTACK SURFACE
Phishing, drive-by downloads, credential theft and malicious ads, as the boundary moved from firewall to browser (Provos et al., 2007; Khonji et al., 2013).

texts.name: Point 16
texts.text:
SIGNATURES FALL BEHIND
Fast-changing domains, hidden payloads and short-lived infrastructure defeat signature-based tools.

texts.name: Point 18
texts.text:
DETECTION GREW SMARTER
Machine learning, then deep learning and Transformers that read URLs in context (Devlin et al., 2019).

texts.name: Point 20
texts.text:
FROM ONE MODEL TO AGENTS
Specialised agents for detection, extraction, analysis and reporting, reasoning step by step like analysts (Yao et al., 2023).

texts.name: Study body
texts.text: A multi-platform, agent-based system that analyses URLs in real time and protects users while they browse. Specialised agents classify the URL, analyse the domain, inspect behaviour, look up threat intelligence and map attacker techniques, then agree one verdict.

texts.name: Subtitle 24
texts.text: Three persistent problems limit AI threat detection for ordinary users and small teams

texts.name: Card body
texts.text: Single-model URL classifiers are prone to false positives. An early CyberForge heuristic rated every URL, google.com included, "medium risk" because of a +0.5 offset. Alert fatigue makes users ignore real threats.

texts.name: Card body
texts.text: A classifier gives a probability, but cannot list the indicators of compromise on the page, map script activity to a MITRE technique, or link the domain to earlier threat reports.

texts.name: Card body
texts.text: No widely deployed open system fans one browser event out to specialised analysers, keeps the result, reuses past visits and shows it on desktop and mobile. SOAR does, at enterprise cost.

texts.name: Answer text
texts.text: CyberForge answers with specialist analysis, inspectable evidence and controlled sharing of results

texts.name: GRQ text
texts.text: How can a multi-agent AI system, organised as a network of specialised analysers, be designed to provide real-time and explainable threat intelligence and protection for URLs and web resources across different platforms?

texts.name: RQ text 34
texts.text: How can URL analysis be divided among different AI agents, and what is the smallest set of agents needed for a reliable threat assessment?

texts.name: RQ text 38
texts.text: How can URL classification, behavioural analysis, IOC extraction, MITRE ATT&CK mapping and threat-intelligence lookup be combined into one consistent, accurate system?

texts.name: RQ text 42
texts.text: What method can combine the agents' results to reduce false alarms while still identifying serious threats when strong evidence is available?

texts.name: RQ text 46
texts.text: How can historical browsing information improve detection, identify recurring malicious activity and strengthen protection over time?

texts.name: GO text
texts.text: Design, implement and evaluate a multi-platform AI-driven system that monitors URLs in real time, detects and explains threats with cooperating agents, and gives timely alerts and protective feedback while keeping historical context and threat records.

texts.name: Card body
texts.text: Decompose URL analysis into coordinated tasks for reliable real-time assessments.

texts.name: Card body
texts.text: Combine content, behaviour, structure and threat intelligence for accuracy and consistency.

texts.name: Card body
texts.text: Cut false alerts while strong malicious indicators still trigger immediate warnings.

texts.name: Card body
texts.text: Link current URL behaviour with known attack patterns and external threat databases.

texts.name: Work finding

texts.name: Work finding

texts.name: Work finding

texts.name: Work finding
texts.text: MITRE ATT&CK: a shared language for attacker tactics and techniques.

texts.name: Work finding
texts.text: URLNet learns URL representations directly from raw text.

texts.name: Work finding
texts.text: BERT: pre-train, then fine-tune; security-adapted variants followed.

texts.name: Work finding
texts.text: ReAct: reason, act, observe, repeat — the loop behind agents.

texts.name: Work finding
texts.text: Generative Agents: memory keeps agents consistent over time.

texts.name: Gap 66
texts.text:
FEW COMPLETE MULTI-AGENT SECURITY SYSTEMS
Frameworks show the idea; few open systems apply it end to end.

texts.name: Answer text
texts.text: A full working pipeline of connected agents

texts.name: Gap 69
texts.text:
MODEL AND SERVICE FAILURE
Systems rarely say when a model or service did not answer.

texts.name: Gap 72
texts.text:
ACCURACY OVER REAL FALSE ALARMS
Lab scores hide how often safe sites are flagged (Sommer & Paxson, 2010).

texts.name: Answer text
texts.text: Multi-signal aggregation for few false alarms

texts.name: Gap 75
texts.text:
HISTORICAL CONTEXT UNUSED
Past observations are rarely reused later (Park et al., 2023).

texts.name: Answer text
texts.text: Memory supplies prior verdicts as context

texts.name: Gap 78
texts.text:
HARD TO REPRODUCE
Private data, closed systems, costly infrastructure.

texts.name: Answer text
texts.text: Public tools and modular, testable services

texts.name: Subtitle 301
texts.text: What the study shows, and what it does not

texts.name: Card body
texts.text: Eight specialist analyses and a Reporter combine complementary evidence into one inspectable, explained verdict, with few false alarms.

texts.name: Card body
texts.text: No single-model ablation: no proof of superiority to one model, universal protection or current production performance.

texts.name: Card body
texts.text: Verified identity and workspaces, five privacy choices, service authentication, device signing and explicit action states.

texts.name: Card body
texts.text: Test account switching, grant revocation, hostile input, replay, expiry and elevation prompts in the packaged product.

texts.name: Card body
texts.text: Validate the five consent categories, URL redaction, deletion and sync withdrawal across every client.

texts.name: Card body
texts.text: Temporal and domain-held-out evaluation; isolated training; reviewed feedback, never unchecked retraining.

texts.name: Card body
texts.text: Verified rollback before broader automatic response; grow CLI and MCP only with permission contracts.

texts.name: Persp text
texts.text: Longer deployments with raw logs · agent ablations · independent regional and hosted-phishing corpora · a blinded explanation study · isolated training · richer CLI and MCP tools · packaged mobile capture · a real dynamic-execution sandbox
